source_grounded_clause_or_inference: **Server** transforms an array of previously published category instances into a computed output **for each configured output container**. The same transformation function may produce **different results based on that container's inputs**. Clients do not own or directly overwrite read-only computed instances.

Inputs record **container number, category name, instance number, publish time and category value**. Computed-category configuration is global for all publishers, **not private per publisher**. The server can trigger recomputation on changed dependent publications.

Clients MUST NOT add **members to private computation input containers 2 or 3** even where the server does not enforce this. Data in those inputs may disclose private per-endpoint state if subscriptions were permitted. Server publishes constrained aggregates to observer-facing containers instead.

**Server** computes **aggregateState** and **aggregateMachineState**, and writes special **legacyInterop** categories for PIDF/MSRTC watchers; legacyInterop **MUST be registered as a private category**. Do not expose raw machine data via legacy PIDF notifications.

For **aggregateMachineState**, server considers only `machineState` category instances whose **expireType is endpoint**. If **none**, aggregateMachineState availability **MUST become 18500 (offline)**. User, static or time-scoped machineState must not win this competition.

When ≥1 eligible machineState exists, **lowest numeric availability** wins; tie → the **most recently published** machineState, and copy selected machineState attributes into aggregateMachineState. Do not sort descending or simply take latest endpoint regardless of availability.

For aggregate availability, collect `state` instances from selected container, **exclude** types `machineState`, `aggregateMachineState`, `aggregateState`, then add computed `aggregateMachineState`. This is a **different set** from winner selection above.

When a state has `manual=true`, discard **other state instances older** than it using `startTime` (or category publicationTime if startTime absent); **aggregateMachineState is exempt** from that filtering. Do not make manual state erase every machine endpoint.

Base **aggregated availability** is the **largest numeric availability** among the retained states. This intentionally differs from the **lowest numeric** machineState selection. Two-stage reduction is required, not a universal `min` or `max`.

If the computed **aggregateMachineState** is **Idle availability class 4500–5999** and base aggregated availability is **Busy 6000–7499**, add **1500** to the aggregated availability to produce resulting **aggregateState** availability. This is conditional, not a blanket idle offset.

Activity selection uses the state set from availability computation; remove activities with **neither token nor custom string** and those outside activity's **minAvailability..maxAvailability**. Winner **MUST have greatest minAvailability**; ties prefer most recent **startTime if present, else publication time**. If none, aggregate activity **SHOULD be empty**, edition note excludes OCS 2007.

For `lastActive`, if **new aggregate availability** is **not** Idle, BusyIdle, Away or Offline → set `lastActive` **empty**. If it **is** one of those classes and **old aggregate availability wasn't**, set lastActive to **server current UTC**. If both previous/new are in these classes, preserve existing lastActive. **This is from the figure, not an inferred paragraph.**

If a single relevant **calendarState** contributes `meetingLocation` or `meetingSubject`, server **MUST use** them; if multiple qualifying calendarState instances exist, aggregated subject/location **MUST be empty**. Never arbitrarily choose first meeting and leak it.

When aggregate availability **<12000**, server **SHOULD** copy endpointLocation/time-zone elements/device type from aggregateMachineState. For **>=12000**, server **can ignore** these fields. This is a *SHOULD* and *can*, not a universal MUST.

Input **container 2** produces **state+legacyInterop** for **100**, **200**, **400**; input **container 3** produces **state+legacyInterop** for **300**. Distinct output detail sets are explicitly defined in multi-page table.

For **100**, state category exposes **aggregate availability only** (plus xsi:type); for **200**, adds activity token, lastActive, device; for **300**, adds **meetingSubject, meetingLocation, endpointLocation, time-zone/device**; for **400**, adds endpointLocation/time-zone/device but **not meetingSubject/Location**. **Do not merge to a universal rich presence payload.**

Server also creates **container 2 aggregateMachineState, instance 0x10000000, expireType user** and **container 2/3 aggregateState**. For generated observer aggregates output `expireType user, instance1` if any machineState exists, or `static, instance0` when none. A computed state may persist as a static fallback even with no live endpoint.

**legacyInterop** per observer container contains aggregate availability only and is used for legacy format generation. **State vs legacyInterop are different category names and may be independently selected** by subscriber protocol.

Server can avoid publishing if computed category equals existing instance (optimization). Client MUST NOT infer “no new NOTIFY” means no recomputation happened; distinct timestamps and event versions still require source-backed handling.

Each endpoint publishes **machineState and device capabilities to private input container 2**. Server MUST trigger **services** aggregation on changed state/device category instances. Computed services published for self to **2**, observers to **100,200,300,400**; server MAY optimize unchanged outputs.

Create set of **distinct URI attributes** from device capabilities; **one service element per distinct URI** (MUST). Duplicate endpoint URIs do **not** imply two service records, but may contribute competing capabilities.

For each URI and capability type, pick winning capability and machineState linked through **endpointId**. Source defines multiple conditions involving `publish`, `render`, `capture`, **capability version**, and **most active endpoint** (lowest availability then newest publishTime); one global boolean `canVideo` is insufficient.

For non-publish (`publish=false`) capabilities, winner is added to **observer services** and **self services**; publish-only capabilities are added to **self services**. Winning endpoint's availability becomes `deviceAvailability`, and self view additionally carries `preferredEndpointId`.

All 4 observer `services` aggregates use **instance0, expireType user** and carry only **render/capture** capability, each SHOULD have `deviceAvailability`. Self **container 2** includes render/capture/**publish** and SHOULD carry `preferredEndpointId` + `deviceAvailability`. This is *purposefully asymmetric*.

Client **MUST** publish `calendarData` **instance0 in container1** for workingHours derivation. Client MUST NOT add members to container1, MUST compare new data with prior to avoid unchanged republishing. Server transforms `WorkingHours` element to **workingHours instance0 in container1**, unpublishes when source removed; avoids identical output. Feature **not supported** in OCS/Communicator 2007/2007 R2.
Client **MUST** publish `state` to containers **2 and 3**, MUST NOT add members there. Server computes `dndState instance0` into containers **2,0,100,200,400** from input2, and **3,300** from input3.

Server examines `userState` / `presentingState`. If qualifying source availability is in **DND 9000–11999**, published dndState availability MUST be **9500**; otherwise **omit availability element**. This is not a copy of arbitrary requested DND number. Feature excluded from OCS/Communicator 2007/2007 R2 per note <47>.

Aggregation subsystem declares **no additional timers, error responses or other local events** in its own section. This does **not** negate SERVICE publish/schema/permission errors in §3.2.5.4 or downstream SUBSCRIBE transaction timers.

Presence server maintains **DelegateSet per delegator**, keyed by **delegate SIP URI** and with **one version number for the whole set**. Each DelegateEntry has **publish** and **redelegate** permission Booleans. Neither is the contact list deltaNum nor category instance version.

Delegator submits SIP **SERVICE** `setDelegate` and operates on **one delegate per request**. Server MUST verify **From URI = To URI**, use this identity to select its DelegateSet, validate XML and require submitted **version = current set version**. On first empty list server version is **0**.
Delegate action **`add`, `modify` or `remove` only**. Delegator **cannot delegate to their own URI**; specified delegate URI **MUST represent valid presentity in deployment**.
`publishOperation` and `redelegateOperation` each accept `authorization=allow|deny`. **Absent operation element means deny**, not an implied inherited authorization or grant.

**`add` on an already existing delegate is valid, updates it**; **`modify` on a missing delegate is also valid, creates it**. `remove` on a nonexisting delegate **MUST be rejected**. These are not generic HTTP PUT/PATCH semantics; treat behavior exactly as specified.

Server SHOULD enforce administratively configurable delegate limit; increments **DelegateSet version only after successful processing**, MUST NOT commit changes before full processing, returns SIP **200 OK** on success.

After successful change server MUST send **NOTIFY or BENOTIFY to each matching self-subscription** whose scope includes delegates, **including sender endpoint**. The `roaming-self+xml` `delegates` child **MUST be complete new set**, **not a partial per-delegate delta**; when empty, send empty delegates body with **updated version**.

Errors: **400** invalid XML, delegate equals delegator; **403 SHOULD** From/To mismatch; **403 MUST** remove missing delegate; **404 MUST** invalid presentity URI; **409 MUST** stale version; **413 MUST** quota exceeded. **Lync Server 2010 note <48>** varies From/To mismatch response, so cannot apply 403 to every historical product.
Delegate management has **no separate protocol-defined timers** in its subsystem. SIP transactions, authentication SA expiry and self subscriptions retain their independent timers.

XSD **`<setDelegates version=unsignedInt><delegate uri=anyURI action=add|remove|modify>`**, optional operation elements each with required `authorization=allow|deny`. This schema is **separate** from `<setContainerMembers>` and MS-SIP `setContact`.

UCS migrates groups/roster **from enhanced presence server to email server contact store**; it is neither an MS-ABS downloadable global address book nor a SIP category container. Server uses MS-SIP §3.7 legacy contact/group data model.

A SIP client able to connect to email server **SHOULD** send roaming-contact `SUBSCRIBE` with `Supported: ms-ucs-ready` to signal migration readiness. Server queues user for migration; **exact start time is implementation-specific**. Product note says this behavior is **only supported by Lync Server 2013** in specified overview application. Do not infer every deployment supports it.

**During migration** the contact/group list becomes **read only**. Server rejects **SERVICE mutations**. A failed `setContact` in this phase is not proof authentication has expired, and retrying rapidly cannot override server migration state.

**After migration**, SIP endpoints that cannot access email server **MUST NOT send ms-ucs in SUBSCRIBE**. Presence server proxies contact list updates; whether full snapshots vs deltas, reads only vs reads+writes are **implementation-specific**. Clients with email-server connectivity **SHOULD include ms-ucs supported**.
UCS failures add **MS-OCER §7.3** diagnostic errors on top of **MS-SIP §3.7** contact-list errors. No new UCS-only timer is defined (§3.10.2/.5).

Client-side contact cache **cannot treat a read-only/migration rejection as authorization to delete contacts or groups**. A full snapshot may legitimately replace delta stream post-migration; cross-protocol reconciliation is **S**, not a fixed RFC event algorithm.

`rpc:ContainerId` = **xs:unsignedShort ≤32767**; `rpc:ContainerIdForSetContainer` = **1..32767** (minExclusive0/maxInclusive32767). Thus **container0 cannot be edited** at XSD level, before server authorization rules.

In `categories` **`uri:xs:anyURI` required**, individual `category name` required; **instance, publishTime, container, version, expireType, endpointId, expires are optional in the general categories-notification schema**. But §2.2.2.1 separately mandates attributes under particular responses; do not let broad XSD optionality override those procedural MUSTs.

`<containers><container id=rpc:ContainerId version=unsignedInt><member type=... value?>`; member types **user/domain/sameEnterprise/federated/publicCloud/everyone**, member `value` optional in base schema; per-type semantic validation remains protocol-driven.

Request root `roamingList` in namespace **`http://schemas.microsoft.com/2006/09/sip/roaming-self`**; required **≥1 `roaming`** from categories/containers/subscribers, optional later **rex:roamingEx** allowing delegates and extension values. Response root **`roamingData`** permits optional **categories, containers, subscribers, delegates** in that order and respective imported namespaces.

Publication root **`publish`** contains exactly **one `publications`** child with **≥1 `publication`**; `publications uri` required. Per-publication **categoryName:string, instance:unsignedInt, version:unsignedInt, container:rpc:ContainerId, expireType enum are required**, `expires:unsignedInt` optional but only legal for `time` per message-processing prose. `xs:any` permits one custom category payload; extension wildcard does not exempt required attributes.

Container mutation root **`setContainerMembers`** has ≥1 container; each has ≥1 member, container id **1..32767** and **version unsignedInt required**. Member action enum **`add|remove`**, **`add` default**, type required; **NOT `delete`**. Any previous research table asserting `action=add|delete` for this exact XML schema is incorrect and **MUST be amended**.

`setSubscribers` schema requires **exactly ONE** subscriber element, `user` required and `acknowledged:boolean` required **fixed true**. This syntactically enforces one acknowledgement per SERVICE; cannot send `acknowledged=false` or a batch.

Self-notification `delegates` has **version unsignedInt required** and delegate entries with **uri anyURI, publish boolean, redelegate boolean all required**. This notification differs from mutation schema's `authorization allow/deny` attributes and add/modify/remove action.

**Internal namespace inconsistency in original:** Section's heading `Location:` says **`.../2008/09/sip/subscription-context` (lowercase)**, but the literal XSD **targetNamespace and xmlns:tns are `.../2008/09/sip/SubscriptionContext` (capital S/C)**; namespaces are case-sensitive. Both exact spellings appear on **PDF p211** (visually confirmed), and cannot be silently normalized. Wire-level interoperability needs authoritative erratum and original example cross-check; **OPEN-NORMATIVE-CONFLICT**.

Subscription context shape can include watcher contactList, optional delegator list, protocol extension `ct:delimiter`, `ct:end`, `ct:extension`; these **do not** establish that any arbitrary contact roster subdata is safe to render as public watcher data. Input context scopes/ACL separately required.

Delegation request uses **`action=add|remove|modify`**, version unsignedInt, `delegate uri` required, operation `authorization=allow|deny`, optional publish/redelegate operation; `modify` missing/delegate and `add` existing behavior is application semantics (3.9), not XSD cardinality.

**Response `categories`** and request `publish/publications` use **different namespace/document roots** and different attribute optionality. A generic `category` XML deserializer that requires request fields in every response will reject allowed protocol notification data.
